Issued at 255 PM EDT Sun Jul 26 2026

Through Tonight...Limited cloud coverage this morning has allowed
for sufficient daytime heating across east central Florida, with 
temperatures already in the low to mid 90s areawide and exceeding 
the convective temperature. As a result, shower and storm activity
has started a bit earlier than CAM guidance initially suggested, 
with increasing coverage anticipated over the next several hours. 
The adequate daytime heating will support modest instability 
across the area, with MLCAPE exceeding 1500 J/kg and likely
increasing through the afternoon hours. DCAPE has already exceeded 
800 J/kg per the 15Z XMR sounding, with guidance indicating some 
spots could exceed 1000 J/kg this afternoon. Interactions between 
outflow from this initial convection and the east coast sea breeze
will be the primary drivers of robust convective development this
afternoon into the evening hours, with storm hazards including 
frequent lightning strikes, wind gusts of 50-60 mph, heavy 
downpours thanks to PWATs exceeding 2" areawide, and a low chance
of small hail. A Marginal Risk (1/5) of severe weather remains in
effect from Titusville to Orlando and areas northward. Showers 
and storms will move offshore today, with the potential for some 
slow-moving activity. In areas that see slower moving showers and 
storms there is a greater risk for localized flooding, with 
rainfall accumulations of 2-5" possible. A majority of east 
central Florida remains under a Marginal Risk (1/4) of excessive 
rainfall today. Activity will gradually diminish and push offshore
through this evening, with some lingering activity across the 
local waters possible overnight. Mostly dry across the peninsula 
tonight, with overnight temperatures in the mid to upper 70s.

Monday-Tuesday...The Florida peninsula will remain under the 
broad influence of ridging aloft through early this week, with the
mid- level high centered across Texas and the Four Corners region
and its eastern ridge axis extending towards Florida. Northward, 
a trough gradually shifts off the east coast, prompting an area of
low pressure just offshore the Mid Atlantic region to push 
farther offshore, with its associated frontal boundary stalling 
across the southeastern US. The Atlantic ridge axis will remain 
south of the Florida peninsula. Locally, the Florida peninsula 
will remain within a plume of moisture through early this week, 
with PWATs exceeding 2.1". Coupled with persistent southwesterly 
winds and limited intrusion inland of the east coast sea breeze, 
higher shower and storm chances will continue to be favored across
the eastern portion of the peninsula, with PoPs ranging between 
30-60%. Modest instability, steep low-level lapse rates, PWATs 
2"+, and DCAPE exceeding 800 J/kg each afternoon will support 
storm development, with primary hazards including frequent 
lightning strikes, wind gusts of 45-55 mph, and heavy downpours 
that could result in some localized flooding. West to northwest 
steering flow will push activity offshore each day, with a 20-40% 
chance of activity persisting across the local Atlantic waters 
through the overnight hours while conditions remain mostly dry 
across the peninsula.

Near to above normal temperatures are forecast to persist across 
east central Florida through early this week, with highs ranging 
from the low to mid 90s on Monday and the low to upper 90s on 
Tuesday. The warmest temperatures will be focused across the 
northern portions of the area. Peak heat indices of 102-107F are 
anticipated areawide, with a low to medium chance of exceeding 
Heat Advisory criteria, especially across the northern counties. 
This will continue to be monitored closely and products will be 
issued as needed. Residents and visitors are encouraged to 
practice heat safety to avoid developing heat-related illness. 
Overnight temperatures will remain warm and muggy in the mid to 
upper 70s, with some spots potentially nearing 80 on Tuesday night
near the metro areas.

Wednesday-Saturday...Mid-level troughing across the eastern US 
will strengthen, with 500 mb heights falling across the Florida 
peninsula mid to late week. A series of shortwaves will pass 
overhead, rounding the base of the trough and pushing southward 
across the Florida peninsula. At the surface, this will help push 
a quasi- stationary boundary draped across the southeastern US 
towards Florida, stalling just north of the area. The pressure 
gradient will tighten starting Wednesday, with southwesterly winds
remaining breezy which will limit the chances for the east coast 
sea breeze to move inland. While the sea breeze won't necessarily 
be the primary driver behind shower and storm development, energy 
from the passing shortwaves aloft will support development across 
east central Florida each day, particularly during the afternoon 
hours from Thursday onward. Rain and storm chances will range
